To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a novel, post-hoc, gradient-based visual explanation method for convolutional neural networks.
we present a novel optimization based method to generate fine-grained, interpretable and valid visual evidence for the predictions of Convolutional Neural Nets.
we present a novel, post-hoc optimization based method to visualize fine-grained and interpretable explanations for CNNs which can be used to defend against adversarially added evidence.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: (1) We propose a post-hoci, optimization based explanation method, which enables explanations which are (a) fine-grained, (b) interpretable and (c) defend against adversarial artifacts, such as adversarial evidence.

the following questions: How can we generate fine-grained, interpretable visual explanations for convolutional neural networks? What are the limitations of the explanations? How can we defend against adversarial artifacts?
the question: How to generate fine-grained, interpretable and reliable visual explanations for convolutional neural networks?

our approach is a valuable tool to gain insight into the behavior of neural networks and their predictions.
the proposed approach is a strong baseline for post-hoc visual explanations.
we provide the first method to explain CNN predictions in terms of fine-grained evidence, which is interpretable, valid and robust.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our method can provide a fine-grained and valid explanation of a prediction, which is interpretable, robust against adversarial evidence, and can be used to validate and debug models.
we provide a new, interpretable, post-hoc visual explanation method, that is able to provide explanations for any model, without the need to change the model.
our method is the most accurate method for explaining CNNs and the only one that is able to explain all types of models, i.e. convolutional and recurrent networks.

our explanations are both more interpretable and more fine-grained compared to existing methods, while still preserving the characteristics of the image.
